title_en: Following Up Without Chasing: How to Stay in Touch So People Are Glad to Hear From You
title_zh: 跟進，而不是追著跑：怎麼保持聯絡，讓對方樂於收到你的訊息
excerpt_en: Most opportunities are lost to silence rather than rejection. The fix is following up properly: often enough to be remembered, kindly enough to be welcome, and always with something worth reading.
excerpt_zh: 大多數機會不是被拒絕，而是在沉默中流失。解法是好好跟進：頻繁到對方記得你，溫和到對方歡迎你，而且每次都帶著值得一讀的東西。
description_en: The difference between following up and chasing is what you bring each time. A practical rhythm for staying in touch with prospects and new customers without pressure.
description_zh: 跟進和追著跑的差別，在於你每一次帶來了什麼。一個實用的節奏，讓你不施壓地與潛在客戶和新客戶保持聯絡。
keywords: follow up, direct selling follow up, customer care, staying in touch, calendar reminders, Mikael Chew, 跟進
blocks: p
Ask a group of builders where their lost opportunities went and most will point to rejection. In my experience, rejection accounts for far fewer of them than silence does.
問一群夥伴：失去的機會都去哪裡了？大多數人會說是被拒絕。在我的經驗裡，被拒絕的遠遠少於在沉默中消失的。
p
Someone said "let me think about it" and nobody called back. A customer had a question in their first week and didn't want to bother anyone. A prospect was interested, then got busy, then forgot.
有人說「讓我想想」，然後再也沒有人回電。有位客戶在第一週有個問題，又不好意思打擾別人。有個潛在客戶本來有興趣，後來忙了，然後忘了。
p
None of those people said no. They simply drifted away while nobody was looking.
這些人沒有一個說過「不」。他們只是在沒有人注意的時候，慢慢漂走了。
h2
Why people stop following up
為什麼大家不跟進
p
Most builders know they should follow up. They avoid it because they're afraid of becoming the person everyone dodges, the one whose name on the screen makes you sigh.
大多數夥伴都知道應該跟進。他們逃避，是因為怕自己變成大家都想躲的那個人，那個名字一出現在螢幕上，就讓人嘆氣的人。
p
That fear is reasonable. Chasing is real, and people do hate it. What separates following up from chasing is simple: what you bring with you each time.
這個擔心是合理的。追著跑確實存在，大家也確實討厭它。跟進和追著跑的差別很簡單：你每一次帶來了什麼。
ul
Chasing asks for something every time. "Have you decided yet?" "Are you ready to order?" Each message takes a little from the other person.
追著跑每一次都在要求。「決定了嗎？」「準備好下單了嗎？」每一則訊息，都從對方身上拿走一點東西。
Following up brings something every time. A useful article, an answer to a question they asked, a genuine check on how they're doing. Each message gives a little.
跟進每一次都帶來東西。一篇有用的文章、他之前問題的答案、一句真心的近況關心。每一則訊息，都給出一點東西。
p
People are glad to hear from someone who gives. They start avoiding someone who only takes.
人們樂於收到願意給予的人的訊息，也會開始躲避只會索取的人。
h2
A rhythm for new customers
新客戶的跟進節奏
p
The first week after someone buys is when they decide whether they made a good choice. A short, predictable rhythm helps them feel looked after without feeling watched.
有人購買後的第一週，是他判斷自己是否做了好選擇的時候。一個簡短、可預期的節奏，讓他感覺被照顧，而不是被盯著。
ul
Day 1: a thank-you, and one line on how to get started.
第1天：一句感謝，加上一句如何開始使用。
Day 4: check it arrived and that they've begun. Answer any question.
第4天：確認收到、已經開始使用，回答任何問題。
Day 7: ask how the first week has been, and listen.
第7天：問問第一週感覺如何，然後好好聽。
Then monthly: something genuinely useful, with no request attached.
之後每月一次：一則真正有用的東西，不附帶任何要求。
h2
A rhythm for "let me think about it"
面對「讓我想想」的節奏
p

When someone says they need time, give them time, and agree when you'll be back in touch. "Of course. Would it help if I checked in next Thursday?" Most people say yes, and now your next message is expected rather than intrusive.
對方說需要時間，就給他時間，並且約好什麼時候再聯絡。「當然。我下週四再問候你一下，好嗎？」大多數人會說好，於是你的下一則訊息，變成被期待的，而不是打擾。
p
When Thursday comes, lead with something useful before you ask anything. If the answer is still "not now", thank them, offer to stay in touch now and then, and mean it.
到了週四，先帶上一點有用的東西，再問任何問題。如果答案仍然是「現在還不行」，謝謝他，表示會偶爾保持聯絡，然後真心做到。
h2
Let a calendar do the remembering
讓日曆幫你記
p
Good intentions don't survive a busy month. The builders who follow up well almost never rely on memory.
好的意圖，撐不過忙碌的一個月。跟進做得好的人，幾乎從不依賴記憶。
p
Put every follow-up into your calendar the moment you agree it, with one line in the notes about what was said last time. Each morning, look at today's list first and handle it before anything else.
每一次約好跟進，當下就放進日曆，備註寫一句上一次聊了什麼。每天早上，先看今天的清單，在做任何其他事之前先處理它。
p
It takes ten minutes a day. Over a year it's the difference between a business full of loose ends and one where nobody falls through the cracks.
一天只要十分鐘。一年下來，這就是「到處都是斷掉的線頭」和「沒有人被遺漏」的事業之間的差別。
p
So think of the last five people who told you "maybe". Do you know exactly when you're next in touch with each of them?
所以，想想最近五位跟你說「再看看」的人。你清楚知道，下一次跟他們每一位聯絡是什麼時候嗎？
